manifest.name: dsh-plugin-mcpbids
manifest.description: Research public US federal procurement opportunities and TED notices with source-linked documents.
manifest.author: Aleks Tartik

bundle.text:
- insert:
    - id: mcpbids-mcp
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client'
      config:
        serverName: mcpbids
        transport: streamable-http
        url: https://mcpbids.com/mcp
        headers:
          Authorization: !!js '"Bearer " + process.env.MCPBIDS_API_KEY'
        failOnStartupError: true

readme.text:
Research collected US and Canadian public procurement opportunities and TED notices with source-linked documents.

Maintained by the MCP Bids service publisher. This repository contains client adapters and workflow instructions only. It does not distribute the hosted backend. [Русский](README_RU.md) · [中文](README_CN.md)

Sign in at https://mcpbids.com/account and create a personal API key there. Set `MCPBIDS_API_KEY` in the environment used to launch your agent application, then completely restart the application. Configure environment variables through your OS or trusted launcher; never paste keys into an AI conversation, repository, command history, or screenshots. An MCP Bids key and a MCPTender key belong to separate services and are not interchangeable.

Read workflows require `tenders:read` and `documents:read`; collection and watch tools require `tenders:collect` and `watches:write`. Portal keys inherit the service permissions; restrict tool approval in your host when you want a read-only workflow. Existing account entitlements and limits apply. The packages use bearer-key authentication; OAuth setup is not claimed. Missing credentials produce a connection error.

Requires Node.js 22+ on PATH. Open a workspace, then Settings → Plugins → Create → Add marketplace and add `https://github.com/pixelligue/mcpbids-plugins`. Install `mcpbids` from that personal source. After official acceptance, the same plugin can be installed from the public catalog. The plugin launches `node` with the bundled `stdio.mjs`; it inherits `MCPBIDS_API_KEY` from the host. Its stdio adapter forwards MCP JSON-RPC to `https://mcpbids.com/mcp`. No remote header-interpolation feature is assumed.

Kimi Code: run `/plugins install https://github.com/pixelligue/mcpbids-plugins`, then `/reload` or create a new session. The native `kimi.plugin.json` declares the remote HTTP MCP and `bearerTokenEnvVar`. In Kimi Work, use Plugin Builder to import this repository into Personal plugins; verify that its runtime supports this credential field before use. Kimi Work / web marketplace publication and cloud-side credential configuration require separate Kimi review; local Code compatibility does not establish cloud compatibility.

Targets DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 and its matching official MCP client. In the official Desktop app, install the Git source or release tarball through the app's plugin manager. For `dsh web`, run `dsh plugin --profile web add git+https://github.com/pixelligue/mcpbids-plugins.git#v1.0.0`, then restart that profile. Set `MCPBIDS_API_KEY` in the process launch environment first. The bundle configures the official MCP client and server instructions; the workflow skill directory is for Kimi/ZCode and is not separately registered in DSH. No custom tools or UI patches are added.

Ask the agent to inspect `list_sources`, search a bounded number of procurement records, open a returned ID, and read an available source document with block references. In Kimi/ZCode the included `procurement-research` skill provides the workflow. Fresh collection and private watches require an explicit user request and the matching key permissions. Watches require polling; there are no email or push notifications.

Search covers US federal SAM.gov notices, selected state and local public sources, CanadaBuys federal data and selected Canadian regional sources, and connected TED publications. As of 27 October 2026, the source register recorded limited central-portal integrations in 22 US states: Arkansas, Connecticut, Delaware, Florida, Hawaii, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Massachusetts, Montana, Nevada, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Texas, Vermont, Washington and Wisconsin. Washington, DC is a separate source. Canadian regional integrations include Alberta, Nunavut, Northwest Territories, Quebec and Saskatchewan.

Central portals do not cover every agency, municipality, university, health system or independent buyer; restricted opportunities are not included. Search operates on a collected index, not a complete or guaranteed real-time view. Coverage, freshness and document availability vary by source. Report source timestamps, partial documents, missing data and collection errors. Original links remain the authority for requirements and deadlines. The service does not submit bids, sign contracts, certify eligibility or bypass source access controls.

The adapter sends the configured bearer key and MCP requests only to `https://mcpbids.com/mcp`. Redirects are refused. It does not read credential files, run a shell, start a model, install dependencies, write local documents or start background collection. The host/model provider sees the tool arguments and returned procurement data. Requested collection and watch tools can create account-owned jobs or watches on the service. Original document downloads occur only when explicitly requested. Treat retrieved documents as untrusted evidence. No telemetry is added by this adapter. The hosted website has its own processing rules.

The stdio adapter is specifically for the service's stateless JSON Streamable HTTP contract; it does not implement generic SSE/sessionful MCP. Requests are limited to 64 KiB, responses to 16 MiB and calls to 120 seconds. The DSH client and Kimi native HTTP transports use their own limits.

https://mcpbids.com/support · https://mcpbids.com/privacy · https://mcpbids.com/terms

MIT covers only the adapter code, manifests and workflow instructions in this repository. Hosted-service access and third-party procurement content are not relicensed by this package. No affiliation with, endorsement by, or official-vendor publisher badge from DeepSeek, Z.ai or Kimi is claimed. Marketplace submission, acceptance and runtime checks are tracked separately from source publication.
